chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Ammar Al-Sabati narrated a report from you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it?' I said, 'He reported that the Sunnah is obligatory.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Where is he going? Where is he going? It is not like this. I narrated to him, rather I said to him: The one who prays and is devoted to his prayer, not distracting himself in it, or not omitting anything in it, Allah turns to him as he turned to it. So perhaps half of it is raised, or a quarter, or a third, or a fifth. And we have only commanded the Sunnah so that by it what is deficient from the obligatory prayer is completed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the purpose of Sunnah prayers in Shia jurisprudence according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects a common misconception by distinguishing Sunnah prayers from obligatory duties, clarifying that their primary function is to perfect the *fard* prayers by compensating for specific deficiencies or distractions. The Imam illustrates that while the obligatory prayer is complete, the voluntary acts serve to elevate the spiritual quality of the worship, with rewards proportionally increased based on the worshipper's focus and devotion. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the complementary nature of *Sunnah* acts as means of spiritual refinement rather than independent legal obligations.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Ammar Al-Sabaty reported from youasws a report’. Heasws said: ‘And what is it?’ I said, ‘He reported that the Sunnah is a necessity’. So heasws said: ‘Where is he going? Where is he going? It is not like this. Iasws narrated to him, rather Iasws said to him: ‘The one who prays and is devoted upon his Salāt, not discussing with himself therein, or does not omit (anything) therein, Allahazwj would Devote upon him what he devoted upon it. So, sometimes a half of it is Raised, or a quarter of it, or a third of it, or a fifth of it, and rather weasws are ordering with the Sunnah for it (the Sunnah Salāt) to (make it) perfect by it what had gone (deficient) from the Obligatory (Salāt)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, "Ammar al-Sabatiy has narrated from you a Hadith.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What Hadith is it? 5 I then said, ‘He narrates that Sunnah is obligatory.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Where does he go! Where does he go! I did not speak to him as such. I only said to him that when performing Salah (prayer) if one is attentive toward it, does not speak to one’s soul in it and does not make mistakes in it, Allah comes forward eagerly to what is performed eagerly. Perhaps one half is raised, one fourth, one third or one fifth is raised. We command to perform Sunnah only to complete what is missed of obligatory ones.’”
